result.architecture_summary: The architecture has a sound kernel—durable state, bounded workers, branch isolation, deterministic checks, Unity runtime evidence, bounded repair, and human design authority—but it is wrapped in a reconciliation-first control plane that has not executed a single persisted task. Direct bounded agent runs produced the door prototype, mana, and camera; subsequent effort largely hardened reconciliation and task bootstrap.
result.verdict_reason: The worker/validation model is fundamentally useful, but milestone ordering, duplicate authorities, and moving-GDD handling are unsound. The next planned milestone adds RAG, scanning, decomposition, artifact authority, generation, and promotion before the pipeline can execute, validate, merge, or complete one already-ready task.
strong_decisions: One bounded task per worker; repository state survives model context loss.
Runtime Unity evidence may override a source-level evaluator PASS.
No-op repair detection and bounded circuit breakers solve observed failures.
Single-worker-first is appropriate for Unity scenes and shared assets.
Implementation workers should not silently make game-design decisions.
Dependency readiness is deterministic rather than reconstructed by an LLM.
structural_flaws: taskcontrol only validates and displays work; it cannot claim, block, invalidate, complete, or execute it.
The graph has no priority or value ranking, so dependency-ready is not equivalent to the best or safest task.
AgentCrew is door-specific and Assignment6GER is camera/Assignment-5-specific; neither consumes Tasks/*.yaml generically.
Milestone 2 bundles many speculative systems although NSC-003 already contains a detailed compact context.
Unity compilation, tests, runtime evidence, and merge-driven completion are documented but not integrated.
Semantic verification declared zero material findings while retaining substantive defects in the approved task candidate.
observed_failure_solutions: Assignment 6 runtime feedback repaired wrong camera direction, absent following, and bad framing after static PASS.
Assignment 6 rejected a Refiner that claimed success without changing Assets.

Reconciliation recovery machinery addresses real max-turn, interrupted-run, identity-order, source-boundary, dangling-dependency, and conflict-merging failures—although these are mostly failures of the chosen reconciliation subsystem.
Assignment 4 critics caught drift in generated tutorial/hint copy, establishing value for content-specific evaluation when such content is actually needed.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Generic project scanner and project-state cache beyond direct repository search.
Progressive decomposition before an actionable oversized task has failed.
Artifact Authority, promotion metadata, and multi-evaluator Artifact GER before a real missing-design artifact exists.
GitHub Projects mirroring, leases, merge queues, continuous scheduling, and parallel worker arbitration.
Repeated full multi-model reconciliation after the bootstrap.
overengineering: Reconciliation contains 10,275 lines of top-level Python and 73,225 lines of committed output across 123 files for a one-time 37-task seed.
TaskGraph contains 2,878 Python lines for JSON-compatible task files and five read-only commands.
Git already preserves history, yet immutable run trees and duplicated mutable current projections are committed.
The 349-line GDD is represented by a 1,537-line hand-maintained RAG snapshot that is already stale.

Separate Planner, Implementer, Validator, semantic auditors, refiners, streaming repair workers, and arbiters are used where one coding agent plus tests and human playtesting previously delivered features.
missing_components: Durable blocked, needs-replan/design-drift, and complete-after-merge transitions.
Stable requirement IDs and a GDD change-impact mechanism.
Unity batch compile/EditMode/PlayMode execution on a machine with Unity.
A compact ignored or external run journal instead of committed model transcripts.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary authorities are reviewed canon/design, integrated main, one durable task ledger, and transient branch/run state.
Reconciliation snapshots duplicate Git history; task bootstrap evidence becomes stale; RAG duplicates the GDD; PROJECT_REQUIREMENTS duplicates process rules embedded in the GDD.
Future GitHub status would duplicate Tasks unless one is strictly a projection.
Merged code and task status can diverge because completion is only a documented rule.
Until real generated design artifacts become common, ordinary reviewed design files and PRs provide the needed authority boundary without a separate Artifact Authority subsystem.
gdd_iteration_concerns: The GDD changed in 13 commits and was repeatedly expanded during reconciliation; synchronization is ongoing, not a bootstrap event.
The canonical GDD is revised 2026-08-21, while the reusable RAG snapshot declares 2026-07-30. Its tests pass because they test the stale snapshot against fixed stale chunk IDs.
Tasks retain free-form section citations but no GDD version/hash, so affected work cannot be found deterministically after a design change.
Only open/complete states exist, leaving no truthful state for completed code invalidated by revised design.

A GDD change should version affected requirements, pause linked active work, mark tasks needs-replan/design-drift, assess merged code/tests, update or obsolete contracts through review, and then resume. It should not silently rebuild the entire graph or preserve old completion unexamined.
result.throughput_assessment: Major near-term leverage is not demonstrated. Assignment 3 delivered the door prototype, Assignment 5 delivered mana, and Assignment 6 delivered the camera. From the August 18 pipeline-plan commit through the frozen commit, there are 147 first-parent commits and no later NoSafeCircle asset commit; 114 touch reconciliation-related material. Current machinery selects seven ready tasks but cannot execute one. With further infrastructure forbidden, the first break is that taskcontrol prints a task and nothing consumes it; next come unavailable automated Unity validation and manual completion state.
human_intervention_points: Choose priorities and approve design changes.
Correct flawed or over-specified task contracts.
Inspect Unity scenes, packages, build settings, visual behavior, feel, and balance.
Resolve architecture-changing blockers and shared-asset conflicts.
Review and merge until automated Unity evidence is trustworthy.
Decide whether completed work is patched, reworked, or obsoleted after canon changes.
Select and judge art, audio, and content quality.

next_slice.title: Deliver NSC-003 end-to-end without another platform layer
next_slice.why: Mouse-directed movement is visible core gameplay and unlocks door and spell work. It forces the actual missing path—input assets, implementation, scene integration, Unity evidence, human feel testing, repair, merge, and state update. Its task file already contains enough context, while the planned RAG is stale.
deliverables: Correct NSC-003 by deduplicating its suspend criterion and adding the verifier-identified owner-controlled approach/move-to-position contract with arrival and cancellation semantics.
Implement click destination, hold steering, shared pointer projection, movement restriction, reset, suspend/re-enable, and door-approach boundaries.
Add focused PlayMode tests for movement, suspension, restriction, reset, pointer projection, and approach cancellation/arrival.
Run Unity compilation and focused tests on the development machine, followed by a short human playtest for feel and camera/door integration.
Merge, manually mark complete, and record elapsed time, model passes, human minutes, and failure causes.
next_slice.proof_of_value: One merged, playable gameplay increment completed in a bounded cycle. Its measured bottlenecks determine the next infrastructure slice; repeat once before generalizing a supervisor.

do_not_build_yet: A new generic RAG service or project-state cache.
Progressive Decomposer and Artifact Authority Gate.
More reconciliation verification, refinement, or recovery layers.
Claims, leases, parallel workers, resource arbitration, or merge queue.
Automatic merge and continuous backlog processing.
Additional style/content machinery without active style-sensitive work.

alternative_architecture.description: Use a thin vertical loop. State: reviewed GDD/decision files with stable requirement IDs, main as implementation truth, one small task ledger with design-impact states, and ignored/external run journals. Planning: a human or one LLM drafts only the next one to three slices from the current GDD diff and repository search, applied through normal review. Execution: an explicit task ID creates an isolated branch/worktree and invokes one coding worker that plans within the task. Validation: cheap checks, Unity batch compilation/tests on the real Unity machine, then risk-based human playtesting; semantic review only where tests cannot decide. Recovery: preserve branch, logs, and evidence; permit bounded repair; then block with a concrete question. Unity changes remain serial around the canonical scene/builder. GDD changes trigger requirement-linked impact review rather than full reconciliation.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It retains the proven correctness boundaries while removing duplicate state and immediately producing gameplay. Each new abstraction must answer a repeated observed failure.

evidence.observation: Records two runtime camera failures after static PASS and one no-op Refiner before successful human Unity validation.
Hardcoded to the Sealed Door Prototype rather than consuming persistent task records.
Coupled to Assignment 5 goal outputs and a camera-specific evaluation path.
Provides only validate, list, show, ready, and graph.
Already contains detailed context but duplicates the suspend obligation and omits the approach interface later flagged by verification.
Reports zero final material findings while retaining duplicate criteria, a missing movement-owner interface, an unconsumed derived requirement, and writer-lock uncertainty.
Declares revised_date 2026-08-21; history contains 13 GDD commits.
Tests fixed chunk IDs without asserting freshness against canonical GDD content or hash.
Top-level Python totals 10,275 lines; committed outputs total 73,225 lines.
Gameplay/editor/test C# totals 1,334 lines; all asset commits came from Assignments 3, 5, and 6, with none after August 18.
Live validation and all inspected smoke tests pass, proving structural correctness but not gameplay throughput.

result.biggest_uncertainty: The repository contains no wall-clock, token-cost, or uncommitted playtest data, so the exact productivity multiplier cannot be quantified. The missing executable path and absence of later gameplay commits still establish the direction of the result.
